deep.reconstruction:
Context. The page is the blank verso of a printed 'Avis de l'éditeur'. The publisher is in Genoa (Ponthenier, Gravier), with agents Mme Veuve Courcier in Paris and Grieshammer in Leipzig. This almost certainly belongs to von Zach's 'Correspondance astronomique' (Genoa, 1818–1826), so the notes date to about 1819–1826. That is the period of Gauss's Copenhagen prize essay on conformal mapping (1822) and the 'Disquisitiones generales circa superficies curvas' (1827).

The previous page (7r) sets up the problem. A surface r(x,y) = (ξ, η, ζ) is mapped conformally ('ähnliche Darstellung') onto the (x,y)-plane. The conditions are r_x·r_x = r_y·r_y = n² and r_x·r_y = 0. Gauss then studies the image of a shortest line (geodesic). He concludes that the image curve has curvature (1/n)·∂n/∂σ = ∂ log n/∂σ, where σ is normal to the curve. This page writes the same geodesic condition in vector form and transforms it.

(1) Top margin. Abbreviations a = ∂ξ/∂x, b = ∂ξ/∂y.

(2) First formula. Here d(...) is the second differential along the curve and dr = r_x dx + r_y dy:
  Σ_{ξ,η,ζ} (∂ξ/∂x dy − ∂ξ/∂y dx) · d(∂ξ/∂x dx + ∂ξ/∂y dy) = 0,
i.e. (r_x dy − r_y dx)·d²r = 0.
The vector t⊥ = r_x dy − r_y dx is tangent to the surface. Its product with dr is
  t⊥·dr = (|r_x|² − |r_y|²) dx dy + (r_x·r_y)(dy² − dx²),
which vanishes by the two conformality conditions (my step). So t⊥ is the in-surface normal of the curve. The equation states that d²r has no component along it, i.e. zero geodesic curvature. This is the shortest-line condition in conformal coordinates. Expanding it gives the previous page's equation
  (dx/ds)·n ∂n/∂y − (dy/ds)·n ∂n/∂x + n²(x'' y' − y'' x') = 0.

(3) Bottom part: eliminating dx, dy in favour of dξ, dη, dζ.
  Conformality gives r_x·dr = n² dx and r_y·dr = n² dy (my step). Hence
  ∂ξ/∂x dy − ∂ξ/∂y dx = [ξ_x(ξ_y dξ + η_y dη + ζ_y dζ) − ξ_y(ξ_x dξ + η_x dη + ζ_x dζ)]/n².
  Gauss writes out the expansion: the right-hand block shows ξ_y(ξ_x dξ + η_x dη + ζ_x dζ) together with the term ξ_x ξ_y dξ that cancels.
  The ξ_x ξ_y dξ terms cancel, leaving his middle expression
  ξ_y(η_x dη + ζ_x dζ) − ξ_x(η_y dη + ζ_y dζ).
  Rearranged, this becomes his boxed coefficient of ddξ:
  dη(η_x ξ_y − ξ_x η_y) + dζ(ζ_x ξ_y − ξ_x ζ_y).
  The analogous coefficients of ddη and ddζ are indicated by '+ + = 0'.
  With N = r_x × r_y (surface normal), this coefficient is exactly (N × dr)_ξ. So the condition, after dropping the factor −1/n², becomes
  (N × dr)·d²r = det(N, dr, d²r) = 0.
  This is the classical, parametrization-free statement that the osculating plane of a geodesic contains the surface normal. Gauss is thus checking that his conformal-coordinate condition agrees with the standard Bernoulli–Euler characterization.

(4) Other scribbles. The line 'a ∂ξ/∂x + b ∂ξ/∂y . dξ dy' is a fragment using the abbreviations a, b; I cannot reconstruct its purpose with certainty. The numbers 61, 52, 5, 28, 16 near the printed text are unrelated arithmetic.
errors: No mathematical errors found. The elimination of dx, dy and the coefficient of ddξ are correct.
The overall factor −1/n² is silently dropped. This is legitimate because the right-hand side is 0.

In the expanded right-hand block the cancelling term ξ_x ξ_y dξ appears to be written with '+' in one place (reading uncertain). It must enter with opposite sign to cancel, which it does in his final coefficient.
The step dx = (r_x·dr)/n², dy = (r_y·dr)/n² is implicit and requires the conformality conditions. The algebraic cancellation itself holds for arbitrary dr.

results.what: Geodesic condition in conformal coordinates: (r_x dy − r_y dx)·d²r = 0, where r_x dy − r_y dx is the in-surface normal to the curve because |r_x| = |r_y| and r_x·r_y = 0.
results.modern_name: Vanishing geodesic curvature (geodesic equation) in isothermal coordinates
results.usually_credited_to: Geodesic equations: Euler (1728/1732); geodesic curvature concept: Gauss (1827), Minding (1830); conformal-metric form: Liouville (1850).

results.what: Elimination of dx, dy using conformality, transforming the condition into det(N, dr, d²r) = 0 with N = r_x × r_y. The coefficient of ddξ is dη(η_xξ_y − ξ_xη_y) + dζ(ζ_xξ_y − ξ_xζ_y) = (N×dr)_ξ.
results.modern_name: Osculating plane of a geodesic contains the surface normal (Bernoulli–Euler characterization)

results.what: Context from the previous page, used here: the plane image of a geodesic under a conformal map with scale n has curvature ∂ log n/∂σ.
results.modern_name: Geodesic curvature under conformal change of metric (special case of Liouville's formula)
results.usually_credited_to: Liouville (1850); Gauss's geodesic curvature work (1827); in map-projection context Gauss is known to have studied it

checkable.asserts: (r_x dy − r_y dx)·dr = (|r_x|²−|r_y|²)dxdy + (r_x·r_y)(dy²−dx²), so it vanishes under the conformality conditions.

checkable.sympy: a1,a2,a3,b1,b2,b3,u1,u2,u3=symbols('a1 a2 a3 b1 b2 b3 u1 u2 u3'); rx=Matrix([a1,a2,a3]); ry=Matrix([b1,b2,b3]); dr=Matrix([u1,u2,u3]); N=rx.cross(ry); simplify(a1*ry.dot(dr) - b1*rx.dot(dr) + N.cross(dr)[0]) == 0
checkable.asserts: ξ_x(r_y·dr) − ξ_y(r_x·dr) = −(N×dr)_ξ identically. This is Gauss's coefficient of ddξ, dη(η_xξ_y−ξ_xη_y)+dζ(ζ_xξ_y−ξ_xζ_y), up to sign.
Expands to 0. Gauss's two written forms of the ddξ-coefficient (middle block and boxed block) agree.
